description: An answer of several tokens, teacher forced: each prompt with its answer appended (`input` a list, joined per row), the head read at the positions that predict the answer's tokens (a scope on the appended answer, `occurrence: -1`, with `before`), and each token scored at its own position. On this tokenizer " Tuesday", " Wednesday" and " Thursday" are three tokens and the other days one, so the read is ragged, one entry per answer token. `nll` is each token's negative log-probability given the right prefix; `seq_nll` sums it per row, the answer's negative log-likelihood; `hit` says whether each token was the most likely one, `exact` whether all of a row's were (its `min`), `per_tok` the fraction that were (its `mean`). The weights are random, so the numbers mean nothing; the alignment is the point.
